questions.question: Which band sang "Bohemian Rhapsody"?
questions.fact: "Bohemian Rhapsody" is almost six minutes long and has no chorus. Record bosses thought it was far too long for radio.

questions.question: How many members did The Beatles have?
questions.fact: The Beatles were John, Paul, George and Ringo, and they are the best-selling band in history.

questions.question: Which singer is known as the "Queen of Pop"?
questions.fact: Madonna is often listed as the best-selling female recording artist of all time.

questions.question: Which country did ABBA come from?
questions.fact: ABBA won Eurovision in 1974 with "Waterloo". The name comes from the first letters of the members' first names.

questions.question: What is the highest female singing voice?
questions.fact: From high to low, women's voices go soprano, mezzo-soprano and alto; men's go tenor, baritone and bass.

questions.question: Which instrument did Jimi Hendrix famously play?
questions.fact: Jimi Hendrix was left-handed and often played a right-handed guitar flipped upside down.

questions.question: Who sang "Thriller"?
questions.fact: "Thriller" is the best-selling album of all time, and its music video was a 14-minute mini horror film.

questions.question: Which composer wrote the "Moonlight Sonata"?
questions.fact: Beethoven didn't call it "Moonlight": a music critic gave it that nickname after Beethoven died.

questions.question: How many strings does a standard violin have?
questions.fact: A violin's four strings are tuned G, D, A and E. The bow is traditionally strung with horsehair.

questions.question: Which singer released the album "21"?
questions.fact: Adele named her albums after her age when she made them: 19, 21, 25 and 30.

questions.question: Which Catalan singer released the albums "El mal querer" and "Motomami"?
questions.fact: Rosalía studied flamenco for years in Barcelona and mixes it with pop, reggaeton and electronic music.

questions.question: "Despacito" was a huge 2017 hit for Luis Fonsi and which artist?
questions.fact: "Despacito" was the first YouTube video to reach 5 billion views.

questions.question: Which large orchestra instrument has 47 strings and pedals?
questions.fact: The harp's seven pedals change the pitch of whole sets of strings at once, so the harpist can play in different keys.

questions.question: What does a metronome do?
questions.fact: Johann Maelzel patented the metronome in 1815, and Beethoven was one of the first composers to add metronome speeds to his music.

questions.question: Which rapper's real name is Marshall Mathers?
questions.fact: Eminem's "Lose Yourself" was the first rap song to win the Oscar for Best Original Song.

questions.question: Which country does reggae music come from?
questions.fact: Bob Marley is reggae's most famous star. His album "Legend" is the best-selling reggae album ever.

questions.question: Which singer is called "the King of Rock and Roll"?
questions.fact: Elvis lived at Graceland in Memphis, now one of the most visited homes in the USA.

questions.question: Which Colombian singer had the hit "Hips Don't Lie"?
questions.fact: Shakira's "Waka Waka" was the official song of the 2010 World Cup, the one Spain won.

questions.question: Flamenco comes from which Spanish region?
questions.fact: UNESCO lists flamenco as part of the world's intangible cultural heritage.

questions.question: Which band released "Wonderwall"?
questions.fact: Oasis were led by brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher from Manchester, and their great rivals were Blur.

questions.question: Which British band had an early hit with "Yellow" in 2000?
questions.fact: Chris Martin has said the title came from spotting the word "Yellow" in a phone book while writing.

questions.question: Taylor Swift's album named after the year she was born is called…
questions.fact: "1989" won the Grammy for Album of the Year, and Taylor Swift later re-recorded it as "1989 (Taylor's Version)".

questions.question: Which group sang "Wannabe" in 1996?
questions.fact: Each Spice Girl had a nickname: Scary, Sporty, Baby, Ginger and Posh.

questions.question: Which instrument is Yo-Yo Ma famous for playing?
questions.fact: Yo-Yo Ma was born in Paris to Chinese parents and has won many Grammy awards.

questions.question: What does "DJ" stand for?
questions.fact: "Disc jockey" started as a name for radio presenters who played records on air.

questions.question: Who composed "The Four Seasons"?
questions.fact: Vivaldi was a priest, nicknamed "the Red Priest" because of his red hair.

questions.question: Which singer is famous for "Purple Rain"?
questions.fact: Prince played most of the instruments on many of his own albums himself.

questions.question: Which musical is about a girl called Maria and rival gangs in New York?
questions.fact: West Side Story is a modern take on Shakespeare's "Romeo and Juliet".

questions.question: Which famous band came from Liverpool?
questions.fact: The Beatles became famous playing at the Cavern Club in Liverpool, which you can still visit today.

questions.question: Rihanna is from which Caribbean island?
questions.fact: Rihanna's full name is Robyn Rihanna Fenty, and she founded the make-up brand Fenty Beauty.

questions.question: What is a group of four musicians called?
questions.fact: A string quartet is two violins, a viola and a cello.

questions.question: How many lines does a standard music staff have?
questions.fact: Notes sit on the five lines and four spaces of the staff.

questions.question: Which band recorded "Hotel California"?
questions.fact: The Eagles' "Their Greatest Hits (1971–1975)" is one of the best-selling albums ever in the USA.

questions.question: Which Swedish DJ made the hit "Wake Me Up"?
questions.fact: Avicii's real name was Tim Bergling. "Wake Me Up" mixed dance music with folk and country guitar.

questions.question: A famous "Stradivarius" is usually which instrument?
questions.fact: Antonio Stradivari made his instruments in Cremona, Italy. His violins can sell for millions of euros today.

questions.question: Which singer was born Stefani Germanotta?
questions.fact: Lady Gaga won an Oscar for "Shallow", her song from "A Star Is Born".

questions.question: Which Puerto Rican artist made the album "Un Verano Sin Ti"?
questions.fact: "Un Verano Sin Ti" was the first all-Spanish-language album nominated for the Grammy for Album of the Year.

questions.question: Ricky Martin's 1998 World Cup anthem was called…
questions.fact: Its chorus "Go, go, go! Allez, allez, allez!" became a football stadium classic.

questions.question: What is the Italian music term for "very loud"?
questions.fact: "Piano" means soft and "forte" means loud, which is why the piano's full name is "pianoforte".

questions.question: Which band made the album "The Dark Side of the Moon"?
questions.fact: The Dark Side of the Moon spent over 900 weeks on the US Billboard 200 album chart.

questions.question: What does a timpanist play?
questions.fact: Timpani can be tuned to a precise note with a pedal that tightens or loosens the drum skin.

questions.question: Which music streaming service was founded in Sweden?
questions.fact: Spotify was launched in Stockholm in 2008 by Daniel Ek and Martin Lorentzon.

questions.question: Which singer is known for "Halo" and "Crazy in Love"?
questions.fact: Beyoncé has won more Grammy awards than any other artist.

questions.question: "Gangnam Style" came from which country?
questions.fact: PSY's "Gangnam Style" was the first YouTube video to pass a billion views, in 2012.

questions.question: Which K-pop group had hits with "Dynamite" and "Butter"?
questions.fact: BTS stands for "Bangtan Sonyeondan", which means "Bulletproof Boy Scouts" in Korean.

questions.question: What is the speed of a piece of music called?
questions.fact: Tempo is measured in beats per minute (BPM). Most pop songs are somewhere between about 100 and 130 BPM.

questions.question: Who was the lead singer of Queen?
questions.fact: Freddie Mercury was born Farrokh Bulsara in Zanzibar, now part of Tanzania.

questions.question: Which Spanish duo sang "Macarena"?
questions.fact: "Macarena" stayed at number one in the USA for 14 weeks in 1996.

questions.question: "Aserejé" (The Ketchup Song) was sung by which group?
questions.fact: Las Ketchup are sisters from Córdoba, daughters of the flamenco guitarist "El Tomate".

questions.question: Who sang "Shape of You"?
questions.fact: "Shape of You" was the first song to pass 3 billion streams on Spotify.

questions.question: Which band sang "Smells Like Teen Spirit"?
questions.fact: The title came from a friend writing "Kurt smells like Teen Spirit", a deodorant brand, on Kurt Cobain's wall.

questions.question: Which brass instrument has a slide?
questions.fact: Moving the slide changes the length of the trombone's tube, and that changes the note.

questions.question: Which singer is nicknamed "The Boss"?
questions.fact: Bruce Springsteen is from New Jersey, and his best-selling album is "Born in the USA".

questions.question: The tango comes from which country?
questions.fact: Tango was born in the late 1800s in the port neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

questions.question: Daft Punk was a duo from which country?
questions.fact: Daft Punk almost always appeared in public wearing robot helmets.

questions.question: Who sang "Bad Guy" in 2019?
questions.fact: Billie Eilish recorded her early hits with her brother Finneas in his bedroom.

questions.question: How many beats are in a bar of a waltz (3/4 time)?
questions.fact: The waltz spread from Austria, and Johann Strauss II's "The Blue Danube" is the most famous one.

questions.question: Which instrument has keys and pipes and is often found in churches?
questions.fact: The biggest church organs have tens of thousands of pipes.

questions.question: Which Beatle wrote and sang "Imagine" as a solo artist?
questions.fact: "Imagine" came out in 1971. The piano John Lennon wrote it on was later bought by George Michael.

questions.question: Which singer calls himself "Mr. Worldwide"?
questions.fact: Pitbull is from Miami and has Cuban roots.

questions.question: Enrique Iglesias's famous singer father is…
questions.fact: Julio Iglesias played in goal for Real Madrid's youth team before a car accident changed his path to music.
